intended_object: The canonical functor (in fact an isomorphism of categories) from the comma category (L^op ↓ R^op) to the opposite of the comma category (R ↓ L). It sends an object (a, b, h : R b → L a) to the object (b, a, h), and it swaps the two components of a morphism. This comes from the docstring and from its use as the inverse in `Comma.opEquiv`.
explanation:
An object of `Comma L.op R.op` consists of a : Aᵒᵖ, b : Bᵒᵖ and a morphism op(L a) ⟶ op(R b). That morphism is the same thing as a morphism R b ⟶ L a, which is exactly the data of an object (b, a, h) of `Comma R L`.

A morphism f : X ⟶ Y in `Comma L.op R.op` has components f.left : X.left ⟶ Y.left in Aᵒᵖ and f.right in Bᵒᵖ. Unopping them gives arrows in the reverse direction. So (f.right.unop, f.left.unop) is a morphism unop Y ⟶ unop X in `Comma R L`, that is, a morphism X ⟶ Y in `(Comma R L)ᵒᵖ`. The commutativity condition is the unop of the original square.

This is the standard canonical identification of the two categories. It is stated for arbitrary categories and functors, which is its natural generality. Its companion functor `opFunctor` and the equivalence `opEquiv` built from it are in the same file, and Mathlib has no other declaration of this functor.
